Hi Sophie — thanks, got your profile. I've sketched two high-level paths below (short summary here, more detail attached):

Summary options (ballpark):
- Conservative (FP16 weights, KV in-GPU): for 65B/32k context we estimate ~120–160 GiB GPU memory needed per replica (so requires multi-GPU model sharding or KV offload).
- Optimized (int8/GPTQ weights + 8-bit KV): can reduce in-GPU footprint to ~40–80 GiB, enabling single 80 GiB-class GPU per replica for inference in many cases.

Key nuance is KV-cache sizing: with 32k context the KV-cache (keys+values) dominates memory. If we keep keys/values in FP16 the cache alone can exceed a single A100-80GB. Quantizing KV storage to 8-bit (or using fp16 weights but int8 KV) drastically changes the commitment.

I'm looping in Kar (karthik) and Soojin for the model-specific memory math and to confirm recommended reserved-pool configuration. We'll produce a 1-page committed-capacity recommendation + an XLS with configurations for Procurement.

Action: we'll send a polished estimate and a recommended reserved pool size by EOD tomorrow.

— Marcus

Folks — adding the model-specific math and concrete options so Sophie/procurement can evaluate tradeoffs. I kept the calc conservative (fp16 default unless we specify otherwise).

Assumptions & formulas (high level):
- KV-cache bytes ~ 2 * L * S * D * B where:
  - L = number of transformer layers
  - S = max sequence length (tokens)
  - D = hidden dimension
  - B = bytes per element (2 for fp16, 1 for 8-bit storage)
  - factor 2 accounts for keys + values

Representative examples (Orpheus-32k variants):
1) 65B variant (assume L=80, D=8192):
   - FP32: 2 * 80 * 32000 * 8192 * 4 ≈ 168 GB (keys+values)
   - FP16: halves → ≈ 84 GB
   - 8-bit KV storage: ≈ 42 GB

2) 13B variant (assume L=40, D=5120):
   - FP16 KV @ 32k → ≈ 24 GB
   - 8-bit KV @ 32k → ≈ 12 GB

Model weights (rough on-device resident):
- 65B FP16 weights ~ 40–50 GB (depends on optimizer/overheads); int8/GPTQ weights ~ 12–20 GB.

Putting it together (approx per-replica in-GPU memory):
- FP16 weights + FP16 KV (65B): 40–50 GB weights + 84 GB KV → ~124–134 GB (exceeds single A100-80/H100-80)
- FP16 weights + 8-bit KV (65B): 40–50 + 42 → ~82–92 GB (fits on 80 GB class only in very tight cases; H100-80 with memory margin might be possible but not recommended for production SLOs)
- int8 weights + 8-bit KV (65B): 12–20 + 42 → ~54–62 GB (comfortably fits on an 80 GB GPU)

Operational levers we recommend for Archetype:
1) Prefer int8/GPTQ weight variant for 65B if model quality is acceptable — big win for single-GPU replicas and reserved pool simplicity.
2) If model quality requires FP16 weights, use KV offload (host DRAM or NVMe-backed offload) to avoid multi-GPU model sharding. Offload adds latency and extra infra (PCIe/host memory) but reduces GPU commitment.
3) Use a mixed pool strategy for the committed contract: reserve N 80GB GPUs (int8 path) + headroom in burst pool for FP16 fallbacks during QC or peak events.

Sizing recommendation for 12 concurrent qps (streaming):
- Int8 weights + 8-bit KV path (preferred): plan for 16–20 dedicated 80GB GPUs for steady-state committed capacity. That accounts for autoscaling headroom, maintenance, and 1.2x buffer on top of pure concurrency math.
- FP16 weights + KV offload (fallback path): reserve additional 6–8 GPUs in a separate pool for high-quality fallback (these can be smaller commitments if KV offload used).

Notes on latency/cost tradeoffs: 8-bit KV and int8 weights reduce cost per token but may increase preprocessing/quantization engineering time (1–3 sprints). KV offload can increase tail latency for long-context responses; we should benchmark with your real prompts.

I've attached a CSV with the raw numbers used in the spreadsheet (kv_cache_calc.csv) and an internal XLS with recommended committed counts (arch_estimate_v1.xlsx).
